title: Find X Value of Array II
summary: Given an array of positive integers and a positive integer k, along with a 2D array of queries, each query specifies an index to update, a start index for a prefix removal, and a value xi.
statement: Given an array of positive integers and a positive integer k, along with a 2D array of queries, each query specifies an index to update, a start index for a prefix removal, and a value xi. Perform an operation to remove any suffix from the array, then update the specified index, and remove the specified prefix. Calculate the x-value for each xi, which is the number of ways to perform the operation such that the product of the remaining elements leaves a remainder of xi modulo k. Return an array of results corresponding to each query.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 positive integers, k <= 5, and updates persist across up to 20,000 queries.
Each [index,value,start,x] first updates nums[index], then fixes removal of indices before start.
Count nonempty prefixes of nums[start:] whose product is congruent to x; return one count per query.
hints: A segment is summarized by its total product and counts of each nonempty prefix-product remainder.
Use an order-preserving segment tree; merging appends right prefixes after the entire left segment.
Point-update the changed value, query the ordered range [start,n), and return its prefix-count entry for x.
The merge summary is associative and contains exactly the data required for any larger segment, so updates and suffix queries stay logarithmic.
editorial: The merge summary is associative and contains exactly the data required for any larger segment, so updates and suffix queries stay logarithmic.

tests.explanation: After each persistent update, the requested suffix start has exactly two qualifying prefix products.
After changing the first value to two, one prefix has remainder two and none has remainder one.
